bill.title: Expedited Removal of Unauthorized Persons.

posted_text:
👮 NC HB 96 — NC Bill Could Let Landlords Quickly Remove Occupants

North Carolina could soon give property owners a faster way to remove someone living on their land without going to court.

This bill creates a process where a landlord or their representative can ask a local law enforcement agency to remove an ‘unauthorized person’ from a residential property.

To do this, the property owner must meet specific conditions, including proving the person has no legal right to be there, hasn’t paid rent, and hasn’t been given permission to stay.

The process involves filing a sworn affidavit with the local court and paying a $25 fee.

Within 24 hours, law enforcement would be required to remove the person.

The bill includes protections for property owners, limiting liability if actions are taken in good faith.

This could significantly speed up the process of removing someone living on private property, but it also raises concerns about potential misuse and the rights of those removed.

Aug. 31, 2026: Placed On Cal For 09/02/2026.
